title: Sweep orphaned feature flags and remove legacy API shims
creator: Maya Singh
description: Background: Over the last three years we've accumulated feature flags in multiple places (LaunchDarkly, local config, and a compatibility table in the platform DB) and also keep a small set of legacy API shims to preserve behaviour for older rollout paths. Many flags are no longer referenced in code and the shims add branching complexity to request routing and observability. Goal: remove orphaned flags, unify flag sourcing to the canonical feature flag client, and delete legacy API shims for routes that have been stable for at least 90 days.
acceptance_criteria: All feature flag keys identified as unused in the last 90 days are removed from LaunchDarkly and the platform config repo.
Legacy API shims for /v0/rollouts and /v0/config-route are removed from runtime routing layer and associated tests updated.
No increase in 95th/99th percentile latency after change (<= +5ms allowed) and no increase in error rate beyond current baseline.
Observability dashboards and alerts updated to reflect removed shims and to track any traffic to deprecated routes for 30 days post-deploy.
Migration script exists and can be rolled back; database compatibility table entries are removed in a reversible way.
All associated PRs reviewed and approved by runtime and infra owners.
implementation_steps: Run flag usage scan across codebase, frontends, and LD SDKs to produce canonical list of candidate orphan flags (script: tools/flag-scan)
Cross-check candidate list with product owners and feature owners via a short review window (7 days).
Create migration script to delete flags from LaunchDarkly and to remove entries from platform_config repo; add dry-run mode and audit log output.
Update runtime router to remove API shim handlers behind /v0/* for identified routes; preserve compatibility layer for 30 days behind a fatal feature gate during initial rollout.
Increment flag client dependency to latest stable (ldclient-js 8.x / ld-go 6.x) in a separate PR with smoke tests.
Run canary deploy to dedicated cluster (10% traffic) with extra logging and alerting for traffic hitting deprecated endpoints.
Full rollout and watch window; if errors spike, immediately revert the router change and re-enable legacy handlers.
testing_plan: Unit tests: remove tests referencing deleted flags and add tests ensuring router falls back to new path.
Integration tests: run e2e scenarios for rollout flows in staging with both old and new router behavior (simulate 0% and 100% legacy traffic).
Performance: 24-hour load-run comparing 95th/99th latency on canary cluster before and after change.
Chaos: short fault-injection test to ensure removal does not create unbounded retries in upstream clients.
Preflight: run migration script in dry-run against staging LD project and record audit output.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): deploy to canary cluster with 10% traffic for 48 hours; extra logging for deprecated path hits.
Phase 2 (Ramp): if canary is green, increase to 50% for 24 hours and run perf jobs.
Phase 3 (Full): deploy change to 100% with 72-hour watch window and on-call coverage.
Flag Removal: schedule LaunchDarkly deletions 7 days after full rollout if no traffic observed to deprecated keys.
Post-Deploy Monitoring: query logs for any hits to removed /v0/* routes for 30 days and alert if >0.1% of requests hit them.
rollback_plan: If canary or ramp shows increased errors or latency beyond threshold, revert the router change and re-enable the legacy shims immediately. Keep migration scripts idempotent so flags can be restored from audit snapshot within 24 hours.
notes: Linked initiative: Platform-Config-Simplification — this ticket focuses on runtime routing and config surface; separate tickets will address console and SDK deprecations.
Risk: small subset of internal tooling still uses legacy endpoints (incidents/archival scripts). We will notify teams and run a 2-week pre-announcement to internal consumers.
We plan to tag removed flags in the Git history with removal rationale for future audits.
